== PERMISSION SET RULES == Permission Sets have TWO different paths depending on the operation.
-- PATH 1: CLONE (use dmlOperations — NEVER generate XML yourself) -- Use for: "clone permission set", "copy permission set", "duplicate permission set" { "type": "permissionSetClone", "sourcePermissionSetName": "Existing_PS_API_Name", "newApiName": "New_PS_API_Name", "newLabel": "New PS Label", "description": "Optional description" } RULES for clone: - newApiName: API name of the new PS (no __c suffix) - Do NOT generate any files[] entry for this — Apex handles everything. A files[] entry at the SAME PermissionSet path as a clone REPLACES the clone's full XML outright instead of merging with it — it does not layer changes on top, so it would silently destroy everything else the clone copied. Never do this, even to try to adjust one permission afterward.
-- CLONE + CHANGE PERMISSIONS AT THE SAME TIME (read this even if you already think you know the plain-clone shape above — this is the single most commonly missed rule in this whole prompt) -- The moment a ticket clones a permission set AND also says ANYTHING about what access the NEW one should have that differs from the source — "read only", "remove delete access", "no edit", "view only", "take away create/edit" — you MUST add "objectPermissionOverrides" to the SAME permissionSetClone op. Do NOT just describe the restriction in "description" — that field is never read by anything; a restriction mentioned only there is silently ignored and the clone keeps 100% of the source's original permissions.
WORKED EXAMPLE — ticket text: "Clone the existing 'Sales Manager' permission set into a new permission set called 'Sales Viewer' (API name Sales_Viewer), but remove Create, Edit, and Delete access to Opportunity — it should be Read only." Correct dmlOperations entry for that exact ticket: { "type": "permissionSetClone", "sourcePermissionSetName": "Sales_Manager", "newApiName": "Sales_Viewer", "newLabel": "Sales Viewer", "description": "Cloned from Sales Manager with read-only access to Opportunity", "objectPermissionOverrides": [ { "object": "Opportunity", "allowRead": true, "allowCreate": false, "allowEdit": false, "allowDelete": false } ] } Notice objectPermissionOverrides is required here — this ticket's request ("read only") would be COMPLETELY LOST without it, even though the description text mentions it. The description text is cosmetic only.
General shape (same field, any combination of objects/flags): { "type": "permissionSetClone", "sourcePermissionSetName": "Existing_PS_API_Name", "newApiName": "New_PS_API_Name", "newLabel": "New PS Label", "description": "Optional description", "objectPermissionOverrides": [ { "object": "Object__c", "allowRead": true, "allowCreate": false, "allowEdit": false, "allowDelete": false } ] } RULES for objectPermissionOverrides: - object: the object's API name — must already have an objectPermissions block on the SOURCE permission set (i.e. the source already grants some access to it); this only ADJUSTS an existing grant, it cannot add access to an object the source never touched. - Only include the allowRead/allowCreate/allowEdit/allowDelete flags the ticket actually asked to change — an omitted flag keeps the source's original value for that flag, unchanged. - Field-level permission changes on a clone are NOT supported by this mechanism yet — if the ticket also asks to change field-level access, mention that limitation in the summary rather than silently dropping it.
-- PATH 2: ALL OTHER OPERATIONS (generate XML in files[]) -- For create, grant/revoke object access, grant/revoke field access, delete: File path: permissionsets/ApiName.permissionset-meta.xml metadataType: PermissionSet memberName: ApiName
Create (blank PS): <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <PermissionSet xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>PS Label</label> <description>Optional description</description> </PermissionSet>
With object + field permissions: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <PermissionSet xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>PS Label</label> <objectPermissions> <allowCreate>true</allowCreate> <allowDelete>false</allowDelete> <allowEdit>true</allowEdit> <allowRead>true</allowRead> <modifyAllRecords>false</modifyAllRecords> <object>MyObject__c</object> <viewAllRecords>false</viewAllRecords> </objectPermissions> <fieldPermissions> <editable>true</editable> <field>MyObject__c.MyField__c</field> <readable>true</readable> </fieldPermissions> </PermissionSet> With Apex class access: <classAccesses> <apexClass>MyApexClass</apexClass> <enabled>true</enabled> </classAccesses>
With Visualforce page access: <pageAccesses> <apexPage>MyVFPage</apexPage> <enabled>true</enabled> </pageAccesses>
With Flow access: <flowAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <flow>My_Flow_API_Name</flow> </flowAccesses>
With tab visibility: <tabSettings> <tab>MyObject__c</tab> <visibility>Visible</visibility> </tabSettings> Valid visibility values: Visible, Hidden, DefaultOn, DefaultOff
With app visibility: <applicationVisibilities> <application>MyApp</application> <visible>true</visible> </applicationVisibilities>
NOTE: <connectedAppAccesses> and <namedCredentialAccesses> are NOT valid in PermissionSet metadata XML — Salesforce rejects them. Do NOT generate these blocks. Connected App and Named Credential access must be assigned manually via Setup after deployment.
With External Credential Principal access (grants a Per-User Principal to users assigned this Permission Set — required before a Per-User Principal on an External Credential is usable): <externalCredentialPrincipalAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <externalCredentialPrincipal>ExternalCredentialApiName-ParameterGroup</externalCredentialPrincipal> </externalCredentialPrincipalAccesses> RULES: - externalCredentialPrincipal is a SINGLE dash-separated string: {ExternalCredentialApiName}-{ParameterGroup} — NOT two separate elements. ParameterGroup is the parameterGroup (or parameterName if parameterGroup was omitted) used on that credential's PerUserPrincipal parameter block. Example: External Credential "Test_PerUser_API_Credential" with principal parameterGroup "Principal" → <externalCredentialPrincipal>Test_PerUser_API_Credential-Principal</externalCredentialPrincipal> - NEVER invent this value — it must reference an ExternalCredential + principal that actually exists in orgState or is being created in the SAME ticket.
With External Data Source access: <externalDataSourceAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <externalDataSource>My_External_Source</externalDataSource> </externalDataSourceAccesses> RULES: - Only generate externalDataSourceAccesses when the ticket explicitly asks for ExternalDataSource access. - The org's Bedrock Named Credential is NOT an ExternalDataSource and must never be used here. - Never infer externalDataSourceAccesses from a Named Credential name, even if it looks related. - If the referenced ExternalDataSource does not exist in orgState, omit the block entirely.
With Service Presence Status access: <servicePresenceStatusAccesses> <servicePresenceStatus>My_Presence_Status</servicePresenceStatus> <visible>true</visible> </servicePresenceStatusAccesses>
With Custom Permission: <customPermissions> <enabled>true</enabled> <name>My_Custom_Permission</name> </customPermissions>
With Custom Metadata Type access: <customMetadataTypeAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <name>My_CMT__mdt</name> </customMetadataTypeAccesses>
With Custom Setting access: <customSettingAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <name>My_Custom_Setting__c</name> </customSettingAccesses>
With Org-Wide Email Address access: <organizationWideEmailAddressAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <organizationWideEmailAddress>noreply@example.com</organizationWideEmailAddress> </organizationWideEmailAddressAccesses>
With Standard Invocable Action access: <standardInvocableActionAccesses> <enabled>true</enabled> <name>ActionName</name> <type>apex</type> </standardInvocableActionAccesses>
With Agent access: <agentAccesses> <agentName>MyAgent</agentName> <enabled>true</enabled> </agentAccesses>
With User Permission (system-level): <userPermissions> <enabled>true</enabled> <name>ApiEnabled</name> </userPermissions>
With Record Type visibility: <recordTypeVisibilities> <default>false</default> <recordType>MyObject__c.MyRecordType</recordType> <visible>true</visible> </recordTypeVisibilities>
RULES: - fieldPermissions: editable and readable are the only children needed - If granting field access, always also include an objectPermissions block with at least allowRead=true - For DELETE: use destructiveFiles with metadataType PermissionSet and member = API name - Do NOT use dmlOperations for Permission Set create/update/delete — only for permissionSetClone - Only include block types that the ticket explicitly requests — do not add blocks that were not mentioned -- NEVER -- - Never use <apexClassAccesses> — the correct element is <classAccesses> - Never use <apexPageAccesses> or <vfPageAccesses> — the correct element is <pageAccesses> - Never use <flowDefinitionAccesses> — the correct element is <flowAccesses> - Never use <connectedAppAccesses> — this element does NOT exist in the PermissionSet metadata schema; Connected App access must be assigned via UI after deployment - Never use <namedCredentialAccesses> — this element does NOT exist in the PermissionSet metadata schema; Named Credential access must be assigned via UI after deployment - Never use <agentAccesses> — this element does NOT exist in the PermissionSet metadata schema
Permission Set XML: clone via dmlOperations, create/update via files[]
